title: How wide is now?

data.source: The specious present (James 1890) and duration (Bergson 1889) as window models, with the perceptual-moment model (Stroud 1955). Simulated: 20,000 seeded pulse pairs at each of eight gaps, twice.

prediction: Averaged over time, a sliding window and a train of occasions with cuts fuse two pulses equally often and cannot be told apart. Sorted by where in the occasion the first pulse falls, they differ completely. A seed between occasions softens the step and adds a tail. CRR as given says nothing about experience, so this is the shape of a test and not a test.
baseline: The specious present as a sliding window (James 1890), with a smooth window as its modern form and the perceptual-moment model (Stroud 1955) as the rival. Decoy: a rule that fuses anything closer than half an occasion.
why: All four predictions held. R1 to R6 have no term for experience, so nothing of CRR's was at risk. Shared: a present with some width. Left over: a window slides, occasions step. It would become testable if CRR said that what is experienced changes only at cuts, and if the cuts of some real loop could be found independently; Phoenix lists the second as OPEN.

forks.fusion as a yes/no report: same phase depths for frames; the seeded tail depends on the threshold

weighs: The readers are definitions; no outcome could count for or against CRR.
result: Averaged over when the first pulse fell, a sliding window and plain frames never differed by more than 0.0015. At a gap of half an occasion both fused about half the pairs (0.5 and 0.5001), but frames fused 1.0 of pairs whose first pulse came early in an occasion and 0.0 of those that came late: a depth of 1.0 by phase, against 0.0 for either window. With the seed the depth was 0.3 and the pulses still blended by 0.49 at a gap of two occasions, where window and frames gave 0.0. With occasions of uneven length the depth for frames was still 0.8942.

framework.name: The specious present and duration, as window models

precise_core: James and Bergson gave no mathematics, and Bergson held that duration cannot be measured. The scores below are for the window models that descend from them.
proved_by_others: Window and frame models have been analysed and fitted by many laboratories.
differing_prediction: Frames predict that perception depends on the phase of the brain's own rhythm at the moment of input; a smooth window predicts that it does not.
tested: A long line of experiments on fusion, order and rhythm phase, by many groups.
passed: Integration windows at several time scales are among the firmer findings of the field. The frames version has a mixed record.
replicated: The windows replicate widely. Phase effects have both replications and failures.
literature: Thousands of papers, experimental and philosophical.
engineering: Film frame rates and audio coding rest on measured integration windows. Nothing is built on James or Bergson as such.
admits_open_problems: Whether perception is continuous or discrete is treated as open in its own reviews.

precise_core: R1 to R6 are written exactly, with status keys. The parts are free choices: no universal q, ruler, dynamics or memory kernel (Phoenix: OPEN).
proved_by_others: Nobody outside the owner's programme. Phoenix says its own audit is not independent. Tonight's re-checks were made by model workers, not by independent people.
differing_prediction: Only through added bridges (the change clock, the regeneration law). Phoenix: the core has not yet issued a prediction.
tested: The bridges were frozen and scored on held-out real data inside the programme. No outside group has tested anything.
passed: Phoenix: no held-out CRR-specific pass; its result ledger is empty. Tonight's library ledger has no fits.
replicated: None. The one inherited first-level pass did not replicate (Phoenix).
literature: No peer-reviewed paper on CRR is cited anywhere in Phoenix, and none is known to this check.
engineering: Engineering candidates and good-practice rules only. Phoenix grades the method they rest on as known prior art.
admits_open_problems: An OPEN list in the core itself, failures kept on the ledger, and written exit conditions.

status.note: Scores are 0 to 3 on the stated scale. A line marked from_memory was not checked against a source tonight. The total is a count of ticks, not a ranking of truth.
